findings: No new product or SQL defect reproduced. Six previously absent acknowledgement-loss scenarios pass against the production store and PostgreSQL/WASM migrations.

execution.scope: 6 new tests; real production store and PostgreSQL/WASM migrations, simulated transport error only after successful SQL commit

impact.limitations: FTS unavailable; named graph context and direct source review used.

coverage: create SQL commits, transport loses acknowledgement: exactly one operation/task/reservation, read-only recovery, ownership and changed-content conflict
start commits: lost acknowledgement never grants reserve or a second claim; recovered operation remains read-only
reserve commits: same call and a second call cannot reopen dispatch; unknown accounting stays unknown
settle commits: same receipt reconciles, conflicting usage fails; observed token total applied once
finalize commits: identical result reconciles, result cannot be replaced, one usage event, unknown monetary amount stays null and reservation retained
cancel-before-create commits: lost acknowledgement does not resurrect operation or invent resource grant

priorGateAlreadyExecuted.note: Existing five native multi-connection cases are not counted as newly executed in this lot.

limits: This new suite uses real PostgreSQL compiled to WASM (PGlite), one backend. It does not prove native multi-connection locking.
Recovery recreates the store adapter over preserved SQL state; database process restart, crash, durability of a remote volume and PostgREST transport are not exercised.
The network error is injected after the real SQL call succeeds; no external provider or paid API is called.
A successful reservation is not an actual provider invoice; test amounts remain fixture observations.
gatesNotRepeated: Full KARTA/site suites: root handles composed qualification.
Existing native PostgreSQL CI suite: already executed on PR100; not repeated for test count.
